title: 2019 AMC 8 Problem 6
statement: There are \(81\) grid points (uniformly spaced) in the square shown in the diagram below, including the points on the edges. Point \(P\) is in the center of the square. Given that point \(Q\) is randomly chosen among the other \(80\) points, what is the probability that the line \(PQ\) is a line of symmetry for the square?

solutions.text:
Note the only lines of symmetry for a square are the two diagonals and the two lines connecting opposite midpoints.

On each symmetry line there are \(8\) grid points other than \(P.\) The four lines intersect only at \(P,\) which is not eligible, so these give \(4 \cdot 8 = 32\) distinct choices for \(Q.\)

The probability is therefore \(\dfrac{32}{80} = \dfrac{2}{5}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Each symmetry line has \(8\) possible points besides \(P\)
